question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 10 m/s.

Ignoring air resistance, what is the maximum height it will reach?

(Assume g = 9.8 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Initial velocity** of the ball is given as **10 m/s**, and it is thrown vertically upward. 
• The maximum height can be determined using the **equation of motion:** v² = u² - 2gh , where: 
• **v** is the final velocity at the maximum height (0 m/s). 
• **u** is the initial velocity (10 m/s). 
• **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (9.8 {m/s}²). 
• **h** is the maximum height (to be calculated). 
• Substitute the values into the equation: 0 = (10)² - 2(9.8)h . 
• Rearranging: h = ((10)²)/(2 times 9.8) . 
• Calculate: h = (100)/(19.6) = 5.10 {m} . 
• **Maximum height reached by the ball is 5.10 m.** 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.* 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Equations of motion:** 
• The equations of motion are used to analyze objects in uniform acceleration. These are: 
• v = u + gt (velocity-time relation). 
• s = ut + (1)/(2)gt² (displacement-time relation). 
• v² = u² - 2gh (velocity-displacement relation). 
• **Gravity:** The acceleration due to gravity ( g ) is a constant value of 9.8 {m/s}² on the Earth’s surface. It acts downward toward the center of the Earth. 
• **Maximum height:** At the maximum height, the velocity of the ball becomes zero ( v = 0 ) because gravity completely decelerates the upward motion. 
• **Ignoring air resistance:** The calculations assume that air resistance is negligible, meaning the only force acting on the ball is gravity. 
• **Practical applications:** Understanding projectile motion is essential in sports, engineering, and physics, such as designing ballistics, rockets, and predicting motion trajectories. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Initial velocity:** The speed at which an object is launched determines its trajectory and maximum height. 
• **Effect of gravity:** Gravity causes the object to decelerate while moving upward and accelerates it while descending. 
• **Zero velocity at maximum height:** The object's upward motion halts momentarily before reversing direction. 
• **Air resistance:** In real-world scenarios, air resistance can significantly affect the motion, but here it is neglected for simplicity. 
• **Equation derivation:** The equations of motion are derived from Newton's laws of motion, providing a mathematical framework for analyzing linear motion under constant acceleration.
